Data completeness: full months, real administrative boundary — 7724 recorded incidents total across 3 months (2026-05–2026-07), queried against Bromley's actual ONS 2021 polygon outline (the same shape shown on the map above), not an approximate circle. This is the complete monthly response from the UK Police API for each month in that window. Day score: 2.3213 weighted incidents/1,000 people, averaged over the last 3 months (89% of the 32-borough average). Night score: 8.7642 weighted incidents/1,000 people, same window (68% of the 32-borough average). Both are normalised by plain 2021 resident population (330,000) — no separate workday/footfall figure exists for Bromley in the ONS's 2011 workday-population release (the most recent one published), so no correction is applied here (ratio 1.0) rather than guessing one. This means Bromley's score may be slightly overstated relative to boroughs where a real commuter/footfall correction could be applied — see methodology. Frequently asked questions

Is Bromley safe?

Based on real, current UK Police data, Wandroz rates Bromley as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in London during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in London at night, relative to the other London boroughs currently on the automated pipeline. The rating comes from 7724 recorded incidents over 3 months (2026-05 to 2026-07), split into a day-weighted score (property crime) and a night-weighted score (violence, robbery, antisocial behaviour).

Is Bromley safe at night?

Bromley's night score is relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in London, based on the categories most relevant after dark (violence, robbery, street theft, public order, antisocial behaviour), normalised by an estimated workday/footfall population rather than plain residents where that data exists, so busy central boroughs aren't overstated as riskier just for having fewer official residents.

What official data is Bromley's rating based on?

7724 recorded incidents from data.police.uk (the UK Police's official open crime API), queried against Bromley's real administrative boundary and covering 3 months (2026-05 to 2026-07) — recomputed from the source data whenever the Met publishes new months, not a one-off snapshot. Full category breakdown is shown further down this page.
